title: Who Says So? Sorting Claims About Paul
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Sort fourteen familiar claims about the apostle Paul by their source: Paul's own letters, Acts only, scholars' inference, or later tradition.

educational.topic: Sources for the Life of Paul
learningObjectives: Differentiate claims about Paul by their source, sorting fourteen statements into Paul's own letters, Acts only, scholars' inference, or later tradition, with at least 11 of 14 correct.
prerequisites: Primary sources and myth versus history (Chapter 4)
The Pauline letters as Paul's own words
Paul as persecutor and the road to Damascus

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Concept classifier: sort statements into source categories with immediate, cited feedback
keyQuestions: Where does this claim about Paul first appear?
Which parts of the familiar story does Paul tell himself?
What do scholars reconstruct that no source states?
commonMisconceptions: Everything familiar about Paul comes from his letters; his birthplace, citizenship, the name Saul, and the light on the road come only from Acts.
If Acts and the letters both say something, it belongs to Acts; Paul's own words come first.
Dates such as the year of Paul's call are stated in a source; they are reconstructed by scholars.
Paul's death by beheading is in the Bible; it is later tradition.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on fourteen statements (mastery: 11 of 14).
Sort each part of a guide's one-sentence summary of Paul's conversion.
